deepDive.sceneSummary: Miller takes a taxi from his hotel to Midori-cho. He tells the driver the destination, gives step-by-step directions along the way (turn right at the traffic light, go straight, stop at the flower shop), confirms the route, and finally pays the fare of 1800 yen.
deepDive.storyExplanation: This conversation covers a complete taxi ride in Japanese, from telling the driver where to go (〜までお願いします) to giving directions using the てください pattern, confirming directions with ですね, and handling payment. It introduces practical vocabulary for directions (信号, 右, まっすぐ, 花屋) and taxi-specific phrases (お願いします, お預かりします). The repeated おかげで items (l14-conv-005 through l14-conv-012) are recording artifacts where the same phrase appears eight times — they may represent scene markers or transitions in the video rather than actual conversational lines.

characters.name: Miller (passenger)
characters.role: Passenger giving directions to the driver

characters.name: Taxi driver
characters.role: Driver responding to requests and confirming

conversationFlow.title: Hailing and stating destination
conversationFlow.explanation: Miller tells the driver his destination using 〜までお願いします. The driver acknowledges with はい.

conversationFlow.title: Getting attention and giving first direction
conversationFlow.explanation: Miller says すみません to get the driver's attention, then asks to turn right at the traffic signal using あの信号を右へ曲がってください.

conversationFlow.title: Scene transitions (recording artifacts)
conversationFlow.explanation: Eight identical おかげで lines appear in the source video — these are likely editing markers or data artifacts rather than actual dialogue, but they serve as transitional phrases meaning 'thanks to you'.

conversationFlow.title: Pointing and confirming direction
conversationFlow.explanation: Miller uses 見てください ('please look') to draw attention, and the driver confirms with 右ですね ('right, isn't it?').

conversationFlow.title: Going straight and final stop
conversationFlow.explanation: Miller confirms they should go straight (まっすぐですか), the driver responds まっすぐいってください, then Miller asks to stop at the flower shop using あの花屋の前で止めてください.

conversationFlow.title: Paying the fare
conversationFlow.explanation: The driver announces the fare (1800円です), Miller hands over money (これでお願いします), the driver acknowledges receipt (3000円お預かりします), and both exchange thanks (ありがとうございました).

lineUsage.japanese: ミドリ町までお願いします
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Standard phrase for telling a taxi driver your destination. まで marks the endpoint, お願いします is a polite request formula.
lineUsage.memoryTip: Think: 'destination + まで + お願いします = please take me to~'

lineUsage.realLifeUse: Universal affirmative response in service encounters.
lineUsage.memoryTip: The most basic Japanese word — easy to remember!

lineUsage.realLifeUse: Used to get someone's attention before making a request, like 'excuse me' in English.
lineUsage.memoryTip: すみません is the Swiss Army knife of Japanese — use it for sorry, excuse me, and thank you.

lineUsage.japanese: あの信号を右へ曲がってください
lineUsage.chineseMeaning: 请在那个红绿灯处右转。
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Giving a turn-by-turn direction to a driver. あの signals a visible landmark, を marks the object, へ indicates direction.
lineUsage.memoryTip: Pattern: landmark + を + direction + へ + 曲がってください

lineUsage.realLifeUse: This phrase means 'thanks to you' and is used to express gratitude for someone's help. These 8 repeated lines (l14-conv-005 through l14-conv-012) appear to be recording artifacts from the source video rather than distinct conversational lines.
lineUsage.memoryTip: おかげで = thanks to you. These lines may be scene markers in the video rather than actual conversation. One entry covers all 8 identical items.

lineUsage.realLifeUse: Used to get someone to look at something, like pointing something out to the driver.
lineUsage.memoryTip: 見て is the te-form of 見ます + ください = 'please look'

lineUsage.realLifeUse: Confirmation check using ですね, which seeks agreement. Common in conversation to verify understanding.
Asking for confirmation about going straight. ですか turns a noun/adverb into a polite question.
lineUsage.memoryTip: まっすぐ = straight + ですか = question

lineUsage.japanese: まっすぐいってください
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Asking the driver to continue straight. いって is the te-form of 行きます (go).
lineUsage.memoryTip: まっすぐ + いってください = 'please go straight'

lineUsage.japanese: あの花屋の前で止めてください
lineUsage.chineseMeaning: 请在那家花店前停一下。
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Asking the driver to stop at a specific location. あの = 'that over there', の前で = 'in front of', 止めて = te-form of 止めます.
lineUsage.memoryTip: Landmark + の前で + 止めてください = 'please stop in front of [landmark]'

lineUsage.realLifeUse: Standard way to state a price. Number + 円 + です.
Handing over money or a payment method. これで = 'with this', お願いします = polite request.
lineUsage.memoryTip: これで + お願いします = 'with this, please'

lineUsage.realLifeUse: What a cashier says when receiving money. お預かりします is a humble form of 預かる (to keep/hold).
lineUsage.memoryTip: お預かりします is polite service language (keigo) — used by cashiers and waitstaff.

lineUsage.japanese: ありがとうございました
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Past-tense thank you, used after a service is completed.
lineUsage.memoryTip: Use ありがとうございました (past tense) after the service, ありがとうございます (present) before/during.

lineUsage.japanese: ありがとうございました
lineUsage.realLifeUse: Same as above — both driver and passenger exchange thanks at the end of the ride.
lineUsage.memoryTip: Same as l14-conv-022. It's common for both parties to thank each other.
